items.title: The President: Election, Term & Powers
items.body:
The President (Art 52) is the head of State and nominal executive; real power rests with the Council of Ministers, whose advice is binding (Art 74, made binding by the 42nd & 44th Amendments).

**Election (Art 54-55):** indirect, by an electoral college of elected MPs and elected members of State/specified-UT Assemblies, using **proportional representation by single transferable vote** and secret ballot. Term: 5 years (Art 56), re-election allowed; oath by the CJI.

**Key powers**

| Power | Provision |
|---|---|
| Ordinance when Parliament not in session | Art 123 |
| Assent / veto on bills | Art 111 |
| Pardon (incl. death & court-martial) | Art 72 |
| Emergencies | Art 352 / 356 / 360 |

**Veto types:** absolute (withhold assent), suspensive (return a bill; Parliament can override), pocket (no action). No veto over Constitutional Amendment Bills.
keyPoints: President is elected indirectly by an electoral college using single transferable vote (Art 54-55).
Term of the President is 5 years (Art 56), with re-election permitted; oath administered by the CJI.
Article 123 gives the President ordinance-making power when Parliament is not in session.
Article 72 pardoning power uniquely covers death sentences and court-martial sentences, unlike a Governor's.
Three emergencies: National (Art 352), President's Rule (Art 356), Financial (Art 360).
items.source: APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Central Government (President)

items.title: Vice-President, PM & Council of Ministers
items.body:
**Vice-President (Art 63-71):** second-highest office; ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Art 64); elected by both Houses' members via STV; acts as President for a maximum of six months on a vacancy. Removal is initiated **only in the Rajya Sabha** (effective majority, 14 days' notice), agreed to by the Lok Sabha — no formal impeachment.

**Prime Minister (Art 75):** appointed by the President; by convention the majority-party leader. A non-member must become an MP within **six months**. Holds office during the pleasure of the President but cannot be dismissed while commanding a Lok Sabha majority.

**Council of Ministers (Art 74/75):** total ministers ≤ **15% of Lok Sabha strength** (91st CAA 2003); collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. The Cabinet is the smaller inner core (15-20) that meets weekly and takes binding policy decisions.
keyPoints: The Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Art 64) and acts as President for max 6 months.
A Vice-President's removal resolution can be initiated only in the Rajya Sabha (Art 67).
The PM is appointed under Art 75; a non-member must enter Parliament within 6 months.
Council of Ministers is capped at 15% of Lok Sabha strength by the 91st CAA, 2003.
Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha; the Cabinet is its smaller inner body.

items.title: Parliament: Lok Sabha vs Rajya Sabha
items.body:
Parliament (Art 79-122) = President + Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha, modelled on the British Westminster system (the President, though not a member of either House, is integral to Parliament).

| Feature | Rajya Sabha | Lok Sabha |
|---|---|---|
| Article | 80 | 81 |
| Max strength | 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated) | 552 |
| Current strength | 245 | 543 |
| Election | Indirect (Assemblies), STV | Direct, first-past-the-post |
| Term | Permanent; 1/3 retire every 2 yrs | 5 years (Art 83) |
| Min age | 30 | 25 |
| Presiding officer | Chairman (Vice-President) | Speaker |

The **104th Amendment (2019)** ended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members. Only the Lok Sabha can pass a no-confidence motion and originate Money Bills; the Rajya Sabha alone can invoke Art 249 (legislate on a State List subject) and Art 312 (create All India Services).
keyPoints: Parliament (Art 79-122) = President + Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha, on the British model.
Lok Sabha max strength 552, term 5 years; Rajya Sabha max 250, permanent with 1/3 retiring every 2 years.
104th Amendment (2019) abolished the nomination of Anglo-Indian members.
Only the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion and originates Money Bills.
Rajya Sabha's exclusive powers: Art 249 (State List law) and Art 312 (All India Services).

items.title: Bills, Money Bills & Joint Sittings
items.body:
**Types of bills**

| Bill | Origin | Rajya Sabha role |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary | Either House | Equal power to amend/reject |
| Money (Art 110) | Lok Sabha only | Recommend only; return in 14 days |
| Financial | Either House | Amend/reject (treated like ordinary) |
| Constitutional Amendment (Art 368) | Either House | Must pass by special majority |

The **Speaker certifies** a bill as a Money Bill and the decision is final. If the Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill within 14 days, it is deemed passed.

**Joint sitting (Art 108):** summoned by the President to resolve a deadlock over an *ordinary* bill; **Money Bills and Constitutional Amendment Bills are excluded**. It is presided over by the Speaker. Only three have occurred: Dowry Prohibition (1961), Banking Service Commission Repeal (1978), and POTA (2002).
keyPoints: Money Bills (Art 110) originate only in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha can only recommend within 14 days.
The Speaker's certification of a Money Bill is final.
Constitutional Amendment Bills need a special majority in each House (Art 368).
Joint sitting (Art 108) is presided over by the Speaker and excludes Money and Amendment Bills.
Only three joint sittings: Dowry Prohibition (1961), Banking Service Commission Repeal (1978), POTA (2002).
items.source: APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Parliament (Lok Sabha) & Sessions of Parliament

items.title: Sessions, Dissolution & Parliamentary Devices
items.body:
**Sessions:** the President summons each House on the Cabinet's advice; the gap between two sessions must not exceed six months (Art 85). Three sessions: Budget, Monsoon, Winter.

| Term | Meaning | Authority |
|---|---|---|
| Adjournment | Short suspension of a sitting | Presiding officer |
| Prorogation | Ends a session | President |
| Dissolution | Ends the Lok Sabha's life | President (on CoM advice) |

On dissolution, most Lok-Sabha-linked bills lapse, **except** a bill passed by both Houses awaiting assent, one notified for a joint sitting, one returned by the President, or a bill pending in the Rajya Sabha not yet passed by the Lok Sabha.

**Devices:** Question Hour (first hour; starred = oral, unstarred = written), **Zero Hour** (Indian innovation since 1962, not in the rules), adjournment motion (50 members), no-confidence vs censure motion, cut motions, Motion of Thanks.
keyPoints: Article 85 mandates a gap of no more than six months between two parliamentary sessions.
Adjournment (presiding officer) vs prorogation (ends session) vs dissolution (ends Lok Sabha's life).
A bill passed by both Houses and awaiting the President's assent does not lapse on dissolution.
Zero Hour is an Indian innovation (since 1962), not mentioned in the rules; Question Hour is the first hour.
A No-Confidence Motion is directed at the whole Council of Ministers; a Censure Motion may target one minister and must state reasons.
items.source: APPSC GK PDF — Indian Polity: Sessions of Parliament & Devices of Parliamentary Proceedings

items.title: Parliamentary Committees & the Union Budget
items.body:
**Financial committees**

| Committee | Composition | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Public Accounts Committee | 22 (15 LS + 7 RS) | Examines CAG reports; post-mortem body (est. 1921) |
| Estimates Committee | 30 (LS only) | Suggests economies (est. 1950) |
| Public Undertakings | 22 (15 LS + 7 RS) | Public enterprises (est. 1964) |

24 **Departmental Standing Committees** (1993), 31 members each (21 LS + 10 RS), scrutinise ministries' Demands for Grants. Recommendations are advisory.

**Budget (Annual Financial Statement, Art 112)** passes through six stages: presentation → general discussion → committee scrutiny → voting on Demands for Grants (Lok Sabha only) → Appropriation Bill (withdrawal from Consolidated Fund) → Finance Bill (taxation). **Cut motions:** Policy (to Re 1), Economy (specified sum), Token (₹100). Undiscussed demands are voted via the **Guillotine**.
keyPoints: PAC has 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS) and examines CAG reports; the Estimates Committee has 30 Lok Sabha members only.
24 Departmental Standing Committees (since 1993) scrutinise ministries; their recommendations are advisory.
The Budget is the Annual Financial Statement under Article 112 and passes through six parliamentary stages.
Only the Lok Sabha votes on Demands for Grants; charged expenditure is non-votable.
Cut motions: Policy Cut (to Re 1), Economy Cut (specified sum), Token Cut (₹100); the Guillotine votes undiscussed demands.

items.title: MPLADS, Administrative Reform & the Deputy Speaker
items.body:
**MPLAD Scheme:** each MP recommends works for **durable community assets**. Funds are **non-lapsable** (carried forward), a fixed share is **earmarked for areas with SC and ST populations**, and **at least 10% of sanctioned works** are **inspected at the district level**.

**Administrative reform:** the **N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar Committee** urged a personnel-management machinery; the **Department of Personnel** was created in **1970 under the Prime Minister** (after the First ARC, 1966).

**Deputy Speaker (Art 93/94):** elected by the Lok Sabha from among its members; removable by an **effective-majority resolution after 14 days' notice**; presides when the Speaker's office is vacant.
keyPoints: MPLADS funds are non-lapsable, for durable community assets, with a share earmarked for SC/ST areas.
At least 10% of MPLADS works are inspected at the district level.
The Department of Personnel was set up in 1970 under the PM; the N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar Committee had urged reform.
The Deputy Speaker (Art 93/94) is elected by the Lok Sabha and removable by an effective-majority resolution.
